A_target.statement:
Under the [[Definition:Curry-Howard Correspondence|Curry-Howard correspondence]], a [[Definition:Type|type]] $A$ is [[Definition:Inhabited Type|inhabited]] {{iff}} the corresponding [[Definition:Proposition|proposition]] $A$ is [[Definition:Provable Statement|provable]] in [[Definition:Intuitionistic Logic|intuitionistic]] [[Definition:Natural Deduction|natural deduction]]:
:$\exists t: \vdash t : A \iff \vdash A$

B_source.statement: A [[Definition:Proposition|proposition]] $A$ is [[Definition:Provable Statement|provable]] {{iff}} there exists a [[Definition:Natural Deduction|natural deduction]] derivation of $A$ from the axioms using the inference rules.

derived.a derivation of A: a well-typed term of type A

validity_conditions: Each logical connective corresponds to a type former (implication/function, conjunction/product, disjunction/sum), and each inference rule to a typing rule.
Under this correspondence, a natural-deduction derivation IS a typing derivation, so proofs and programs are the same objects.
Hence provability of A transports exactly to inhabitation of the type A.
proof_plan:
Match connectives to [[Definition:Type Constructor|type constructors]]:
:$A \implies B$ to the [[Definition:Function Type|function type]] $A \to B$
:$A \land B$ to the [[Definition:Product Type|product type]] $A \times B$
:$A \lor B$ to the [[Definition:Sum Type|sum type]] $A + B$
Match introduction and elimination rules to the typing rules for constructors and destructors: $\implies$-introduction to $\lambda$-abstraction, $\implies$-elimination to application.
By [[Principle of Structural Induction|induction]] on derivations and on typing judgements, a derivation of $A$ reads as a term $t : A$, and conversely.
